tagline: Free, serverless HTML apps that sync peer to peer. No accounts. No backends. No excuses.
principles: Each product is one HTML file. Double-click it, or open it from The Watch. It works offline and from disk.
Two devices find each other through a six-letter code and talk over an encrypted WebRTC channel. PeerJS's free server only introduces them.
Everything lives in your browser's storage, backed up as a file or a link. Nothing is uploaded, because there is nowhere to upload it.
No tiers, no paywalls, no feature gates. Thirty-five products, all free, forever.

items.name: Items (LWW)
items.how: On connect, each device says hello with its whole state. After that, every change travels as a put of the changed items. Each item carries a per-field stamp, so the newer write of each field wins and both people can edit offline.

chunked.name: Chunked items
chunked.how: The items pattern, with items that carry photos (base64 data URIs up to 2 MB) split into 128 KB chunks, sent in order and reassembled before merging.
chunked.conflicts: Per field, last writer wins; a photo is one field

cells.name: Cell delta
cells.how: Only changed cells travel, each with a stamp; the whole sheet travels once at hello.

encrypted.name: Encrypted items
encrypted.how: Entries are AES-256-GCM blobs before they reach storage or the wire. Peers exchange blobs by id and stamp; only a device that knows the passphrase can read them.
encrypted.conflicts: Per entry, last writer wins on the blob

hub.name: Hub
hub.how: One device hosts; any number of guests connect to its code. Guests put their own records; the host merges and puts the merged whole back, so every guest sees everyone.
hub.conflicts: Per field, last writer wins; the host is the relay, not the authority

claims.name: Hidden claims
claims.how: The items pattern, where some fields (who claimed a gift) sync to every device but are never drawn on the device of the person the list is for.

lines.name: Work
lines.dek: The tools everyone pays twenty dollars a month for — except these just open.
lines.about: Notes, a task board, a deck, an encrypted vault, a form, a spreadsheet and a screenshot tool. The original seven, plus Create · Home, the launcher that holds them all.

lines.name: Hobby
lines.dek: A log, a scoresheet, a cut list and a bankroll — one file each, shared with the people you do it with.
lines.about: Built around The Watch's Hobbies desk: dressage, woodworking and poker to start, with room for more. Each tool connects to the one person who matters for that pursuit — a trainer, a shop partner, a study buddy — by a six-letter code.

lines.name: Relationships
lines.dek: For two people, and the people around you.
lines.about: Vision, Together / 90 and Date Night are live today on the Lifestyle desk. The rest of the line fills in the everyday: the people you keep up with, the money you split, the week you share, the gifts you give, and the journal you keep between you.

lines.name: Home & Food
lines.dek: The kitchen, the house and what it all costs.
lines.about: What's in the pantry and what to buy, your own recipe box and the week's dinners, the house's maintenance clock, and a home inventory for the day the insurance company asks. Each one syncs between the two phones in the house.

lines.name: Travel
lines.dek: The trip in your pocket, and the points that paid for it.
lines.about: Weekender finds the weekend; Create carries it. Trip holds the itinerary, confirmations and packing list offline, shared with everyone going. Points keeps the balances, expirations and card credits you'd otherwise forget.

lines.name: Money
lines.dek: A budget two people can keep, and a net worth only you can read.
lines.about: Budget is envelopes and transactions, shared across the household's phones. Net is encrypted like Vault: accounts and balances by month, a chart, and a passphrase that never leaves your head.

lines.name: Garage
lines.dek: Every car's history, and the one you're building.
lines.about: Garage is the service log, parts bin and reminder clock for the cars you keep. Rebuild is the project file for the one on jack stands — work packages, parts, hours and a budget against reality — exportable as a page like the Cars desk's own build files.

lines.name: Sports & Games
lines.dek: The pool, the bracket and the scorecard, with no app to install.
lines.about: Pool runs a pick'em, survivor pool or bracket among friends: the commissioner hosts, everyone else joins with the code. Scorebook keeps score for golf, bowling, cards and board games, with every player's history.

lines.name: Body
lines.about: Train is a workout log with programs, PRs and a trainer who can see it. Streak is habits: a grid of days, a chain not to break, shared with the one person who'll ask.

products.desc: Accounts and their balances by month — checking, brokerage, the house, the mortgage — a net worth line, and allocation. Encrypted like Vault, so the file and the sync carry only ciphertext.
functions: Accounts by type: cash, invested, property, debt
Monthly balances and the net worth line
Allocation and change over the year
Passphrase unlock, auto-lock
Encrypted sync between your own devices
Export encrypted JSON or decrypted CSV
specs: Charts drawn after decrypt, in memory
model: S = { v:1, dev, partner, salt, verify,
items: { id: { id, iv, blob, del, _t } } }
// blob → { kind:'account', name, type, order } | { kind:'balance', account, month:'YYYY-MM', cents }

products.name: Create · Garage
products.tag: Every car's history, in the glovebox.
products.desc: The service log for the cars you keep: mileage, what was done, parts with part numbers and where they came from, costs, receipts as photos, and reminders by miles or months. Share a car with its co-owner, or with the shop.
functions: Vehicles with VIN, year and mileage
Service records with parts, part numbers and sources
Reminders by miles or months
Costs by year and by system
Documents and receipts as photos
Export a car's history as a page
specs: Reminders computed from the latest odometer
Parts catalog grows from your own records
model: S = { v:1, dev, partner,
cars: { id: { id, name, year, make, model, vin, miles, _t } },
items: { id: { id, car, kind:'service', on, miles, what, parts:[{name,pn,src,cents}], labor, shop, note, img, del, _t } |
{ id, kind:'remind', car, what, everyMiles, everyMonths, _t } } }

products.name: Create · Rebuild
products.tag: The build sheet for the car on jack stands.
products.desc: A project file like the Cars desk's own: what you paid, the damage, work packages with parts, hours and a budget against reality, before-and-after photos, and the value against comparable sales. Publish it as a page when it's done.
functions: The car and what it cost to buy
Work packages: scope, parts, hours, budget, actual
Parts list with sources and status
Photo log by package
Value: what it's worth against your all-in
Export the build as a standalone page
specs: Same shape as news/garage/*.json build files
model: S = { v:1, dev, partner, car:{ name, paid, damage, comps:[], _t },
items: { id: { id, kind:'package', name, scope, budget, spent, hours, status, order, del, _t } |
{ id, kind:'part', pkg, name, src, cents, status, _t } |
{ id, kind:'photo', pkg, img, caption, on, _t } } }

products.name: Create · Pool
products.tag: Run the pool. Skip the spreadsheet.
products.desc: A pick'em, survivor pool or bracket among friends. The commissioner hosts and sets the games; everyone else opens the link, joins with the code and submits picks. Results typed in once; standings for everyone.
functions: Pick'em (straight or against the spread), survivor, bracket
Commissioner sets the slate; players submit by code
Picks lock at kickoff
Results and standings, tiebreakers
Season history
Export standings as a page
specs: Lock times enforced on the host
The Sports desk's schedule can seed a slate (inbox)
model: S = { v:1, dev, role, host, pool:{ name, kind, _t }, players:{ id:{ id, name, dev, _t } },
items: { id: { id, kind:'game', week, away, home, spread, kickoff, winner, _t } |
{ id, kind:'pick', player, game, pick, at, _t } } }

products.name: Create · Scorebook
products.tag: Keep score. Keep the history.
products.desc: Scorekeeping for the games you actually play: golf with handicaps, bowling frames, euchre, hearts and spades, and any board game by rounds. Every player's record over the years. Share a scorecard to the other phone at the table.
functions: Golf: holes, pars, handicaps, net and gross
Bowling: frames with strikes and spares scored
Cards: euchre, hearts, spades, cribbage by rounds
Any game: players, rounds, a target
Player histories and head-to-heads
Export a scorecard as a page
specs: Game rules are data (a scorer per game)
Works with one phone passed around
model: S = { v:1, dev, partner, players:{ id:{ id, name, hcp, _t } },
items: { id: { id, game, on, place, players:[ids], rounds:[[score]], meta:{}, winner, del, _t } } }

products.name: Create · Train
products.tag: The log a trainer can read.
products.desc: A workout log with programs: exercises, sets, reps and weight, or time and distance; PRs noticed as they happen; a week's plan to follow. Your trainer connects by code, sees the log and adjusts the program.
functions: Programs with days and exercises
Log sets, reps, weight, time, distance
PRs by exercise, volume by week
Trainer view by code, with program edits
Timers for rest and intervals
Export CSV or JSON
model: S = { v:1, dev, me, partner, names,
programs: { id: { id, name, days:[{name, exercises:[{name, sets, reps, note}]}], _t } },
items: { id: { id, on, program, day, sets:[{ex, reps, kg, secs, m}], note, by, del, _t } } }

products.name: Create · Streak
products.tag: Don't break the chain.
products.desc: Habits as a grid of days: tap today, watch the chain grow, see the year. Share with the one person who'll ask how it's going; they see your grid and you see theirs.
functions: Habits with a color and a target per week
Tap a day; long-press to note it
Chains, best chains, the year grid
A partner's habits beside yours
Reminders as a daily page you open
Export CSV
specs: A day is a field, so partial syncs merge
Tiny: the whole app is the grid
model: S = { v:1, dev, me, partner, names,
items: { id: { id, name, color, perWeek, by, days:{ 'YYYY-MM-DD': 1 }, notes:{}, del, _t } } }

gate: Single .html file — the only external scripts are PeerJS (and qrcode-generator) from a CDN, and Google Fonts
Opens from file:// (double-click) and from the hosted page
Works fully offline; PeerJS failing to load degrades to solo mode with a visible note
All data under one localStorage key (create.<id>.v1); inbox under create.<id>.inbox
Backup and restore: JSON file export and import; a link when the state is small enough
Pair by six-letter code: dial, hello, merge, put; a device not seen before must be let in
No console errors in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge
Touch-usable on a phone; 44 px targets; safe-area insets
